subject: Information Theory
title: Morse Code and Efficiency
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Morse Code and Efficiency.

hook.text: E is a single dot in Morse code. Q is dash-dash-dot-dash. Morse assigned shorter codes to common letters in 1838.

buildup.text: Morse estimated letter frequencies from a printer's type case—more E tiles than Q tiles—and coded accordingly.

discovery.text: This is a variable-length code: frequent symbols get short sequences, rare ones get long sequences.

twist.text: Morse code isn't optimal—Huffman coding does better—but it was a remarkable intuitive leap toward information theory.

climax.text: Shannon formalized what Morse felt: optimal coding matches code length to symbol probability.

punchline.text: Common letters, short codes. Morse figured it out by counting type.

quiz.question: Why is E just a dot in Morse code?
options: E is the most common letter, so it gets the shortest code
